summary.headline: Dixon Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR15,557 crore, but EBITDA of INR472 crore (ex fair value gain) and PAT of INR218 crore reflect margin compression as Mobile PLI 1 expired.
summary.overview: Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was INR15,557 crore, with EBITDA of INR472 crore and PAT after minority interest of INR218 crore, both excluding the fair value gain on the Aditya Infotech stake. Management attributed the margin compression to the expiry of Mobile PLI 1 in March 2026 and to input cost pass-through, which lowers percentage margins optically, mainly in mobile and IT hardware. Management guided against margin recovery in the current fiscal and pointed to FY28 for component-led margin improvement. Working capital absorbed roughly INR800 crore in the quarter, which management called temporary, linked to strategic inventory build and payouts of end-March cash.

segments.name: Mobile and other EMS
segments.commentary: Revenue INR14,179 crore and operating profit INR373 crore; volumes fell in line with a 10-12% smartphone market contraction, while Dixon gained share. Management guided Q2 order book of 9-9.2 million units ex-Vivo, taking H1 to about 16-16.5 million against 32-33 million last year.

segments.name: Telecom and networking
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR2,100 crore, flat QoQ, with operating margin about 5.1%. FY27 telecom revenue guided at INR6,700-7,000 crore, up from INR5,000 crore previously cited, with a Gwalior telecom zone MoU and Gemtek optical transceiver JV in progress.

segments.name: IT hardware
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR1,350 crore in Q1, versus about the full FY26 level per management. Margins described as slightly lower than mobile. Inventec 60:40 JV factory expected operational by end-Q3 or Q4 FY27; SSD line installed.

segments.name: Home appliances
segments.commentary: Revenue INR382 crore with operating profit INR32 crore; washing machine and refrigerator margins hit by polymer prices and FX. Refrigerator capacity to rise from about 1.5 million to about 3 million units, and Tirupati adds 0.3 million washing machine units per annum.

segments.name: Consumer electronics (LED TV, refrigerators, IFPD)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR987 crore with operating profit INR58 crore; LED TV mid-range demand soft on memory price inflation. Mini LED production started, with an OEM model by Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Lighting (Signify JV)
segments.commentary: Management cited robust revenue growth in indoor lighting; baton capacity raised to 5 million units per month. Export deliveries to a large US retail chain and a German retailer are expected in Q2 and Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Components (display, camera modules via Q Tech)
segments.commentary: Q Tech camera module capacity to rise from 70 million to 180-190 million units over 15-18 months. Display facility trials start early Q3 and mass production end-Q3 or early Q4 FY27; management does not expect meaningful display contribution until next year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects no margin improvement in FY27 given ongoing memory price pressure; margin improvement is expected in FY28.
Smartphone volumes: Q2 FY27 expected to rise 20-25% QoQ from Q1 volumes; H1 about 16-16.5 million units ex-Vivo; FY27 volume held near last year's 32-33 million.
Vivo JV (PN3 approval received July 2026) expected to close within about two months and contribute from Q3 FY27.
Noida 1 million sq ft facility for the anchor customer expected to commence operations from Q3 FY27.
Display facility trials from start of Q3 FY27; mass production end-Q3 to early Q4 FY27.
PLI 2.0 expected to be effective from 1 April 2026 with FY26 as base year; guidelines awaited within a couple of weeks. Management expects export volumes to build over a couple of quarters.
Export potential from two anchor customers estimated at 15-20 million additional units in a couple of years, about INR18,000-20,000 crore of revenue.
capex_capacity: Chennai IT hardware campus targeted at about 2 million units; Inventec JV factory operational by end-Q3 or early Q4 FY27; SSD line installed; server manufacturing planned from Q3 FY27 subject to partner discussions.

Refrigerator capacity expansion from about 1.5 million to about 3.2 million units at a single site; side-by-side refrigerators in a couple of months; frost-free 240 and 280 litre models, deep freezers and mini coolers by Q4 FY27.
Rexxam Dixon Electronics new Chennai facility operational from August 2026.
Hearables and Wearables JV expanding into dash cams, smart washers, power banks and mobile accessories.
demand_pricing: Smartphone industry volumes declined modestly while market value grew, driven by memory and component price inflation; the broader smartphone market is down 10-12% in volume per management.
Telecom growth driven by 5G, FWA and broadband; new microwave backhaul radio production for a global brand, with exports expected this fiscal.
LED TV demand soft in value and mid-range segments; demand for 50-inch-plus and premium QLED/OLED remained relatively healthy.
Refrigerator industry demand weakened in Q1 from older-inventory liquidation, weak summer and unseasonal rains; order book healthy in direct cool and mini bars.
Management said export mobile margins should be similar to domestic margins.
Management noted PLI 2.0 has a 2.5-5% incentive band on production value and 1.5% for localization (0.3% per component on export value across five components).

qa_highlights.question: Will PLI 2.0 incentives apply to Vivo volumes and how much will Dixon retain?
qa_highlights.answer: Eligibility is brand-wise, measured on incremental production above the FY26 threshold for each brand. Management declined to comment on retention rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the Q1 working capital build of roughly INR800 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited strategic inventory build due to memory supply challenges, plus payment of end-March floating cash to creditors, and called it temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q Tech margin outlook versus its pre-acquisition 6-8% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q Tech is adding margin but below expectations, due to slow capacity build and FX; it expects quarter-on-quarter improvement. Q Tech contributed about INR500 crore in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: When will margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect margin improvement in the current fiscal given memory price pressure; margin improvement is expected in FY28 as components ramp.

qa_highlights.question: What is the telecom and IT hardware outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Telecom FY27 guided at INR6,700-7,000 crore; IT hardware Q1 about INR1,300-odd crore, close to the full FY26 level. Telecom margin about 5.1%; IT hardware margin slightly below mobile.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export opportunity under PLI 2.0 and how fast will it ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Current quarterly exports are about INR1,100 crore; management expects export volumes to build over a couple of quarters, with a long-run potential of INR18,000-20,000 crore.

risks_watch: Memory and component price inflation may keep margins under pressure through FY27.
Mobile volume recovery depends on Q2 order book conversion (9-9.2 million units ex-Vivo) and on the wider market contracting by a double-digit percentage this year.
PLI 2.0 final guidelines pending; incentive retention rate undisclosed.
Working capital outflow of about INR800 crore in Q1; management says it will reverse, so Q2 cash conversion is a watch item.
Vivo JV consummation and Chinese approval reports, plus Q3 consolidation timing.
Display plant ramp (trials from early Q3, mass production end-Q3 or early Q4), with contribution not meaningful until FY28.
Management provided limited detail on precision engineering and the industrial EMS opportunity.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth, PLI 2.0 and the order book, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins, which management guided flat for FY27. Management avoided specifics on retention rates, precision engineering, and the Vivo incentive treatment, and deferred some details to the PLI 2.0 guidelines expected within weeks.
